title: Kansas City Current Win First NWSL Championship, 2-1 Over Washington Spirit — and MLS Cup Playoffs Open with Upsets
excerpt: Vanessa DiBernardo scored directly from a corner kick and Debinha added a late winner as the Kansas City Current beat the Washington Spirit 2-1 for the club's first NWSL title, while Columbus stunned Lionel Messi's Inter Miami 3-0 to open the MLS Cup playoffs.
content:
WASHINGTON — The Kansas City Current are National Women's Soccer League champions for the first time. Vanessa DiBernardo scored directly from a corner kick in the 54th minute and Debinha added a stoppage-time goal as Kansas City beat the Washington Spirit 2-1 in the NWSL Championship on Saturday night at Audi Field, in front of a sellout crowd of 19,365.

DiBernardo's goal — an Olimpico, scored straight from the corner flag — broke open a tense final and stood as the difference until the frantic finish. Debinha, who entered as a substitute in the 81st minute, raced onto a pass from Temwa Chawinga and rounded goalkeeper Aubrey Kingsbury to make it 2-0 in the seventh minute of second-half stoppage time. Trinity Rodman pulled one back for Washington two minutes later, heading home a feed from Tara Rudd in the 98th minute, but the Spirit could not find an equalizer.

DiBernardo was named championship MVP. The veteran midfielder gave birth to her first child in January and returned from maternity leave in July, then scored the goal that delivered the title.

The championship is the first in the Current's history since the club joined the NWSL as an expansion franchise in 2021, and the third NWSL championship overall for Kansas City — FC Kansas City won the title in 2014 and 2015. Kansas City closed the season on an eight-match winning streak, beating Angel City FC 1-0 in extra time in the quarterfinals and Shield winners Gotham FC 2-1 in the semifinals.

For Washington, it was a third consecutive defeat in the league final — this time on the Spirit's home field. The Spirit are now 1-4 all-time in NWSL Championship matches, and the first U.S. professional soccer club since the mid-2000s New England Revolution to lose three straight league finals. Rodman's late header was her first career goal in four NWSL Championship appearances.

The MLS Cup playoffs also opened this weekend, and the first round brought upsets. On Saturday, the seventh-seeded Columbus Crew stunned defending champions Inter Miami 3-0 at home, with Gonzalo Tapia scoring twice, Taha Habroune adding a goal, and goalkeeper Patrick Schulte making five saves — including a stop on a Lionel Messi free kick — as 10-man Miami fell behind 1-0 in the best-of-three series.

Also on Saturday, FC Dallas beat the Portland Timbers 3-0 behind two second-half goals in two minutes from Joaquín Valiente, and 19-year-old Peyton Miller scored twice as the New England Revolution beat the Philadelphia Union 2-0. Miller became the fifth-youngest player to score a goal in MLS Cup playoffs history.

On Sunday, ninth-seeded FC Cincinnati stunned Supporters' Shield winners Nashville SC 1-0 on the road, with a seventh-minute own goal by Patrick Yazbek proving decisive and goalkeeper Roman Celentano making six saves. Nashville had been unbeaten at home all season. Charlotte FC edged the Chicago Fire 2-1 on a stoppage-time penalty rebound from Pep Biel, and the Vancouver Whitecaps — the Western Conference's top seed — beat Real Salt Lake 2-0 on goals from Edier Ocampo and Bruno Caicedo.

The playoffs began Nov. 19 and conclude with MLS Cup 2026 on Dec. 18. The second games of the first-round series are set for next Saturday, with Columbus, Dallas, New England, Cincinnati, Charlotte and Vancouver all one win away from the conference semifinals.
